title: Medium Launches TK App With AI Writing Assistant Integration
summary: Medium's new TK app integrates AI assistance directly into the writing process with @TK prompts, editorial feedback, and transparency features for authors.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 9, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Medium launched TK, a new web app that embeds AI assistance into writing via @TK prompts for research, editing, and style guidance.
- The app addresses AI transparency concerns by letting authors publish notes explaining exactly how AI was used in their content creation.
- TK is free for Medium account holders and supports collaboration, optional Claude agent integration, and human feedback on early drafts.


Medium officially launched TK on November 9, 2026, a standalone writing application that brings artificial intelligence directly into the editorial workflow. The platform lets writers invoke AI assistance by typing @TK followed by their request, embedding help within the writing environment rather than requiring context switching to separate tools.


## How the TK Writing Assistant Works


The app takes its name from the journalism placeholder "TK" (to come), which editors use to mark incomplete information. In Medium's implementation, TK transforms from a gap marker into an active assistant. Writers can ask questions that would normally require research tabs, like date calculations or fact verification. The system also retrieves previously saved notes and draft fragments, helping authors build on earlier thinking without manual searching.


TK ships with specialized capabilities for editorial feedback, headline optimization, and style guide matching for Medium publications. The app can optionally connect to personal AI agents through TK's MCP server or Claude skill integration, allowing the assistant to access project context and stored ideas from the user's broader agent memory.


## Release Date and Availability


Medium officially launched TK on November 9, 2026, making it available immediately on the web platform. The company indicated a desktop application is on the development roadmap. The tool is free for anyone with a Medium account, part of the profitable company's strategy to expand its writing ecosystem without subscription barriers.


## Addressing AI Transparency Concerns


The launch comes as the publishing industry grapples with AI's role in content creation. Multiple authors have lost book deals over suspected AI use, while literary awards face scrutiny when winners appear to have employed automated assistance. Medium acknowledges these tensions by building transparency mechanisms directly into TK.


The app allows authors to publish explanatory notes detailing exactly how AI contributed to their writing. According to Medium, this represents "the start of what we believe is required to publish in the AI era, which is to make the provenance of writing clear, transparent, and inspectable, right down to the prompting and source material." The company positions this as a middle path between banning AI tools and allowing unchecked automation.


- Authors can document specific AI prompts used during drafting
- Transparency notes explain which sections received AI assistance versus human composition
- The system aims to distinguish between AI as a writing aid versus AI as the primary author


## Collaboration and Organization Features


Beyond AI assistance, TK functions as a collaborative writing environment. The social layer lets writers share early drafts with peers for human feedback, combining algorithmic suggestions with traditional editorial input. The app remembers and organizes previous writing, suggests prompts when users face creative blocks, and supports Markdown import and export for compatibility with other tools.


Writing in TK is not encrypted, reflecting its design philosophy around collaboration rather than private journaling. Users can set access control permissions to manage who sees their work in progress. Medium frames the app as a tool that "amplifies human intelligence" using the written word as its foundation, rather than replacing human creativity.


## What This Means for Writers and Publishers


TK represents a bet that transparent AI assistance will become standard in professional writing, rather than a controversial shortcut. By building provenance tracking into the core workflow, Medium positions itself ahead of potential regulatory requirements around AI disclosure in published content. The free tier and Claude integration suggest the platform views AI writing tools as an acquisition channel for its broader publishing ecosystem, rather than a standalone revenue product. Writers gain efficiency without leaving their editing environment, while Medium gains data on how creators actually use AI in the writing process, information that could shape future product decisions.
